The check was computed (it is in the `.json`), its result is large — 155,733 of 904,433 required single sites (17.2%; NOT 22.4%, AND 22.0%, XOR and EQU 18.7%) and 132,435 of 276,926 minimal pairs for NOT alone stop the task **without cutting every route** — and the `.md` reports neither the numbers nor the check, nor lists the omission in §6 departures. The `.md`'s substitute ("the other 17% are the IO reads that set the rotation, stack switches, control instructions and register choices") measures a different thing (the *credited* route), and leaves unnoticed the sites that lie in the credited route yet leave another route standing: for them the task stops for another reason than the removal of the task's computing instructions, which is what the owner's first question asks about. | Plan §3: "**Removal against route**: whether each minimal removal set cuts every route of the sum (contains at least one site of each route's instructions, register choices or controls)"; plan §5: "**Against (1)** … removal sets that do not cut the routes the trace shows (the sum stops for another reason)". `.json` (NOT): `"ablation_against_routes": {"single site in every route": 51535, "single site not in every route": 14842, "pair cuts every route": 144491, "pair does not cut every route": 132435}`. §2 of the `.md` reports only `"required sites in the credited route"`. | Add to §2, after the "Required instructions against the route" paragraph: "Of the required single sites, 82.8% over the nine tasks (from 78.0% for NOT to 88.1% for NAND) lie in **every** route of the task, and 17.2% stop the task with some route left standing — the stop then works through the input rotation, the control flow, or a register choice, not through the removal of a computing instruction of every route (`ablation_against_routes` in the `.json`, per task); of the minimal pairs, 47.8% (NOT) do not cut every route." Add to §6: "The plan's removal-against-route check is reported only in the `.json` (`ablation_against_routes`)." |
| X1.2 | `2 … .md` §2.1 (NOT worked example); `3 plain words.md` §3 | The required site "15 `nop-C`" is presented amid the route's instructions (11, 12, 16, 20, 21, 26) with the gloss "the register choice of the instruction before it", but the pop at 16 — whose wiring the example is explaining — has its own marker at 17, which is **not** required and is not mentioned. Site 15 is the register choice of the `dec` at 14, an instruction outside the route (the `.json` says so); the plain-words file, read by the owner, says only "the marker at 15" in a story that names no other candidate, so the owner will take it for the pop's marker, wrongly. | `.json` `worked_examples.NOT.required_instructions`: `{"site": 15, "instruction": "nop-C", "role": "register or head choice of an instruction outside the routes"}`; same block, `minimal_pairs`, site 14 = `dec`, `"operation outside the routes"`. §2.1 itself: "site 16 `pop` (with `nop-C` at 17)" — so 17 exists and is not in the required list. Plain words §3: "**five** of them stop NOT … the marker at 15 …". | In §2.1: "15 `nop-C`, the register choice of the `dec` at 14, an instruction outside the route: ablated, the `dec` takes one from BX instead, so the later `nand` combines B−1 with B and the output is no longer NOT (the pop's own marker at 17 is not required: without it the `nand` still combines B with 0, and the task is carried by the later hand-out at 34 — the same covering as for site 26)". Say the same in plain words §3; or, if the covering claim is not the reason found, rerun the two ablations (15 and 17) in the scratch space and report what each does. |
| X1.3 | `2 … .md` §4, last sentence | The concluding sentence says more than was tested: "the same letters are a circuit for a task **only** given Avida's meanings for them, its `IO` channel and its rotation of inputs". Only two other meanings for the `nand` letter (`nor`, `and`) and three random reassignments of the 26 meanings were tried; `only` claims the result for every other possible assignment. | §4 table: the rows are `nor`, `and`, `IO` as `nop-X`, input changes, three shufflings — nothing else; §7 "Not tested" does not list other single-meaning changes either way. | "…are a circuit for a task under Avida's meanings for them, and under none of the other meanings tried (`nor`, `and`, three random reassignments of the 26, `IO` as a no-op); other single changes of meaning were not tried." |
| X1.4 | `2 … .md` §4, bullet "The input and output channel"; plan §4 E2 | E2's result ("no program performs any task") cannot come out otherwise: Avida credits a task only at an `IO` output, so with `IO` made a no-op the credit is impossible whatever the program computes. The plan itself predicted "no sum at all" from that rule ("every route begins and ends at `IO`"). As written, the row is presented as showing the *sums* depend on the channel; it shows the *credit* depends on it. | Plan §4 E2: "Prediction …, no sum at all (every route begins and ends at `IO`)". `2 … .md` §0: "read `IO` as doing nothing and no task is performed by any program", offered as part of "what it depends on". | Add to §4: "With `IO` doing nothing no task can be credited on Avida's own rule (credit is given only at an `IO` output), so this row shows the credit's dependence on the channel; that the computation itself also stops is not separately shown. | X1.6 | `2 … .md` §2, "By role" paragraph | The roles list omits **constant-making** — instructions whose only executed work on the route is to make a constant (ZERO, ONES) the circuit uses — though it is 6.3% of NOT's required sites weighted by program (7,140 of ≈114,000) and appears in every task's `.json` role table, larger than several roles the paragraph does name. | X1.7 | `2 … .md` §2, "What the programs share across runs" | "The same kinds and roles, **in every run** (the two tables above)" — the two tables are pooled over all nine runs and cannot show a per-run claim; no per-run breakdown is in the `.md` or the `.json` (which holds only `runs_with_doers`). | The two tables (§2) carry no run column; `.json` per task: `"runs_with_doers": [all nine]` only. | Either add a per-run breakdown of the kinds and roles to the `.json` and cite it, or reword: "across the nine runs pooled; a per-run split was not made". |
